target.title: fix(codex,telegram,tui,cli): keep text truncation UTF-16 safe at four remaining call sites
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four text truncation helpers still use raw `String.prototype.slice()` without surrogate-pair awareness. These operate on content that can contain emoji (user messages, Telegram updates, shell output, session history):

1. **`extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts`** — `truncateText()` truncates Codex prompt text for context projections
2. **`extensions/telegram/src/bot-core.ts`** — raw update logger truncates Telegram message JSON at 8,000 chars
3. **`src/tui/tui-local-shell.ts`** — `appendWithCap` and the close-handler tail truncation drop older shell output
4. **`src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts`** — `buildCliSessionHistoryPrompt()` truncates reseeded session history (4 sites: 1 prefix, 3 tail)

## Why This Change Was Made

Each site now imports `truncateUtf16Safe` or `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. For tail truncation (negative index), `sliceUtf16Safe` is used; for prefix truncation, `truncateUtf16Safe`.

## User Impact

- Codex context projection prompts keep emoji intact
- Telegram raw update debug logs keep emoji intact
- TUI local shell output display keeps emoji intact at the boundary
- CLI session reseed history keeps emoji intact

No behavior change for ASCII text.

## Evidence

- 3 new test cases in `context-engine-projection.test.ts` — surrogate-safe truncation
- 1 new test case in `session-history.test.ts` — emoji in reseed prompts stays intact
- `truncateText` in `context-engine-projection.ts` and `truncateShortTermSnippet` / `truncatePromotedSnippet` in `short-term-promotion.ts` exported for direct testing
